newsitem.title: UK: Huizenga's Republic drives into Europe with U.K. buy.
newsitem.headline: Huizenga's Republic drives into Europe with U.K. buy.

text.p: U.S. billionaire H. Wayne Huizenga's Republic Industries Inc., marking its first major inroad into Europe's car rental market, agreed Monday to buy EuroDollar (Holdings) Plc Plc for about 95.1 million pounds ($151 million),
Republic's cash offer valued EuroDollar at 190 pence per share -- a 60 percent premium to Friday's closing price -- and was recommended by both companies' boards.

"Eurodollar is close to being the jewel in the crown as far as Europe is concerned. It's a tremendous opportunity for us in terms of our global expansion into the car rental industry," said Geoff Corbett, managing director of Republic's European car rental division.
EuroDollar's shares raced ahead on heavy volumes, advancing 69.5 pence to 188 to top the list of percentage gainers on the London Stock Exchange.
Corbett told Reuters he expected trans-Atlantic traffic to boost business at EuroDollar, which currently relies on UK residents for about 95 percent of its business in Britain.
"That's where we see the upside opportunity -- in generating inbound volumes to boost EuroDollar's total revenues in the UK," he said in an interview.

"Because (North American customers) are already doing business with our existing brands in the U.S., we see that we have the opportunity to persuade those people to rent from EuroDollar in the UK," he added.

Republic, headed by Blockbuster Video chain founder Huizenga, has ploughed into the car rental industry in the past year, buying U.S. chains National Car Rental System and Alamo Rent-A-Car, which also has European operations.
Republic's worldwide car rental revenues totalled about $2.8 billion, representing about 30 percent of its total sales, Corbett said.

EuroDollar posted pretax profits of 8.25 million pounds ($13 million) on revenues of 107.4 million ($170 million) last year. It has 110 locations Britain and 320 in the rest of Europe, most of which are franchises.
Corbett said he saw no need for staff cuts or restructuring at EuroDollar.
"It's a very tightly managed, well-run company. Management is going to stay in place and we don't see any surplus fat or cutting to be done in this organisation," he said.
